Etna 1.5 (build 7)

Headphone meetings now transcribe live, and a failed summary is no longer lost — Etna rebuilds it from the saved transcript.

  • Lost summaries recover themselves: when a meeting-end summary fails (network drop, provider outage), the finished card offers "Try Again" — and on the next launch Etna quietly rebuilds summaries for recent meetings whose transcript was saved without one.
  • Remote speech shows up live during headphone meetings: attributed "Speaker N" bubbles appear within moments of someone talking instead of filling in only after Stop, and a warning appears if Etna is hearing a call but capturing no words from it.
  • Speaker naming and attribution no longer drift as a meeting runs long — a clock-rate correction keeps live transcripts aligned with the real audio.
  • AirPods and other Bluetooth headsets: remote voices are no longer garbled into fragments when another app holds the microphone (e.g. Zoom), and system-audio capture recovers cleanly when the output device changes mid-call.
  • The notch level indicator now animates on remote speech too, not just your own voice.
  • A momentary network blip at meeting end no longer costs you the summary — cloud summaries, titles, and classification retry once after a short pause.

Etna 1.4 (build 6)

Person pages that keep themselves current, and a speaker layer that recognizes people far more reliably.

  • Profile highlights: each person's note grows a Highlights section on its own — their role, what they're working on, decisions they made, who they work with — distilled from your meetings and kept current, quietly retiring anything stale. On by default under "Keep people notes updated" in Settings → Automation, with its own sub-toggle.
  • "Sounds like…": when a returning voice matches a remembered colleague closely but not certainly, the speaker row offers the name for a one-tap confirm — and confirming it now actually sticks, so that person is recognized automatically from the next meeting on.
  • Voice recognition now measures how long someone actually talked rather than how much clean audio reached it, so people who spoke plenty stop being invisible to voice memory.
  • The speaking indicator no longer drops out mid-sentence when the diarizer strains, and recurring large meetings are remembered again — they had been stuck on the capped four-slot engine by a state-reset bug.
  • Large meetings say so: a caption explains that live speaking indicators aren't available there, and the honest "labels are refined afterward" notice appears the moment all four slots fill.
  • Zoom: a quiet row suggests opening the Participants panel when names aren't readable, and Spanish and Russian interface decorations are now recognized alongside English. Accessibility permission is asked for at meeting start instead of a poll cycle late.

Etna 1.3 (build 5)

Notes before the meeting starts, a redesigned onboarding, and a clearer Summary setup.

  • Pre-meeting notes: a notes icon in the notch's top-left corner opens a scratchpad before anything is recording — and you keep typing on the same Notes tab once the meeting starts. Type "- " for bullets, ⌘B/⌘I for bold and italic.
  • Summary settings, rebuilt around brand tiles: pick Apple Intelligence, Claude, OpenAI, or Gemini as your summarizer, with key status and setup right below the tiles.
  • Onboarding, redesigned: the Etna stone up front, more breathing room, provider tiles on the AI step, and Skip tucked into the notch's corner.
  • Settings panes that need your attention — a missing permission, a folder that isn't a vault — now show an orange dot in the sidebar.
  • A returning speaker is recognized as themselves instead of appearing as a duplicate "Speaker N", and a half-edited name can no longer stick by accident.
  • Meetings where nothing was transcribed end with a calm one-line notice, and first launch now suggests transcription languages from your keyboard layouts.
